messages:
alex: quick heads up — after merging the kernel-router heuristic change (PR #7391) we're getting a spike in KV slab fragmentation on longctx jobs. multiple hosts hit OOMs in canary, memory usage jumps ~20% and eviction rates look noisy. telemetry link: https://telemetry.internal/kv/frag?id=pr-7391 :alarm_clock:

mira: ugh. which hosts/instance types? can you paste the short logs?

alex: canary group: rtx-pool-3, rtx-pool-5. sample from host rtx-pool-3-12: 
```
2026-03-10T14:02:31Z WARN kv_evict: slab_frag=0.62 resident=64.2GB free=3.4GB inflight_allocs=18
2026-03-10T14:02:31Z ERROR oom: longctx_seq=10240 alloc_request=1.8GB
2026-03-10T14:02:31Z INFO kernel_router: selected_kernel=fastpath_v2 batch_boundary=128
```

sam: thanks. this smells like the new greedy eviction window interacting badly with the kernel's batch splitting. we saw something vaguely similar in staging with sequence-specific allocation patterns. do we have flame graphs?

jia: ran perf on the canary host for 60s, attaching top traces. main thing is heavy allocator churn in slab_allocator::split_slab, lots of small residuals. export: /tmp/frag-trace-rtx-pool-3-12.svg (uploaded to infra).

mira: deploy-bot, status on the rollout?

deploy-bot: Rollout halted — 7391 to canary group flagged by automatic healthcheck (oom_rate > 3x baseline). Ticket: #INT-7420.

sam: can we bisect to the exact commit? alex, do you still have the PR diff? maybe the kernel selection patch or the eviction-window heuristic touched the same path.

alex: PR diff: changed kernel selection to prefer fastpath_v2 for batch sizes > 64 and also adjusted batch boundary calc to floor(seq_len/64)*64. eviction change: greedy window expanded to 3x previous. both merged in same PR.

mira: hypothesis: fastpath_v2 reduces per-token compute but increases intermediate KV writes leading to fragmentation for long contexts. if batch boundary rounding groups long sequences into more frequent slab splits we get more partial slabs.

jia: confirmed: comparing allocations before/after — pre-merge: avg slab_util ~0.78, post-merge: avg slab_util ~0.54 for seqlen>8k. Also seeing 30% increase in small free fragments (<4MB).

sam: plan: 1) rollback eviction window expansion (cheap), 2) run a tiny canary with kernel selection turned off, 3) bisect to separate lines. any objections?

alex: +1 to rollback. I can open a fast rollback PR for the eviction change now.

mira: also add a targeted perf test to CI that runs synthetic longctx traces to catch this — current CI didn't cover >8k tokens workloads.

infrabot: CI perf alert: perf/batching-longctx test regressed by 18% in the merge that included PR #7391. Link: https://ci.internal/build/98123

sam: can someone run the short bisect? candidate commits: a) kernel selection tweak, b) batch boundary floor, c) eviction window expand. if eviction rollback fixes OOMs, we still need follow-up to tune kernel selection.

alex: pushed rollback PR: #7402 (eviction window revert). applying to canary group now.

deploy-bot: PR #7402 applied to canary group: rtx-pool-3 and rtx-pool-5. healthchecks will run for 10 minutes.

mira: meanwhile, add a telemetry probe to measure slab_util and frag_small_pct on every deploy so we can detect this earlier. alex / jia can you add that?

jia: already instrumented locally, will open PR to emit slab_util and frag_small_pct into /ops/kv-metrics.

alex: small note — kernel selection code also logs kernel_choice reasons now; I'll add a quick flag to revert to legacy kernel selection as an emergency toggle (runtime flag) if needed.

sam: good. post-rollback plan: once canary stabilizes for 30m, we need to bisect kernel selection vs batch-boundary change in staging. also add longctx perf test to CI as mira suggested.

mira: can we also add a one-off job to compact fragments on affected hosts? if we can defragment without restart it helps recovery. infra, any ops play?

infrabot: defrag job available: /ops/kv/compact --pool rtx-pool-3 --target-free-percent 15. Recommend running after rollout observed stable for 10m.

alex: ack. thanks all. I'll monitor telemetry and post updates. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — keeping rollout on hold until we see good slab_util and stable OOM rates.

mira: add postmortem checklist item: ensure future kernel selection changes have a canary perf gate that includes longctx convs.

alex: will do. updates in ~15m when rollback healthcheck completes.
